scope: 2026-10-04 literature screening only; representation lane; 10 screened records are NOT 10 accepted methods
common_transfer_contract: Only L[256] and already-read C[B,GA,GT,GV][512 forward dimensions each]; preserve role/head identities, availability and padding masks; first-history-empty case bypasses. Readout-only residual or input adapter; no Memory read/write/query changes, no task-head/loss changes, no extra data, no cross-batch statistics. Any acceptance below means a research candidate, not implemented, smoke-tested, or effective.

candidates.title: KAN: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
candidates.mechanism: Each edge i→j carries its own learned univariate B-spline plus base-function residual; sum edge functions at each output, then compose at least two such layers. Each input coordinate therefore contributes different learned functions to different outputs; this is not replacing a shared MLP activation. Fixed B-spline grid and coefficient training suffice for the numerical forward chain.
candidates.transfer: Project each fixed role separately, mask absent role projections, append explicit availability bits, concatenate with L projection. Use two numerical KAN layers, e.g. 64→32→64, and decode a residual into original readout slots. Disable sample-driven grid updates, symbolic fitting, pruning objectives and auxiliary regularizers; task supervision only. Bounds use fixed per-example transforms, never batch percentile adaptation.
candidates.novelty_difference: Old spline module is an alternating invertible coordinate coupling conditioned on the untouched half. KAN is a noninvertible multivariate function decomposition by edge-specific functions and nested sums, without coupling masks, density Jacobians, or adaptive feature selection.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: A compact composition of local univariate responses could fit nonlinear feature interactions with a different inductive bias from dense Flat. No claim that learned coordinates are interpretable or that MOSI improves.
candidates.risk: Spline support and parameter count can cause poor extrapolation and overfitting. Removing symbolic/regularization workflows loses those paper benefits. A single shared activation replacement must not be counted as this candidate.
candidates.code_evidence: Read raw KANLayer.py: KANLayer.forward calls coef2curve, applies per-edge scale_base/scale_sp and mask, then torch.sum(dim=1). update_grid_from_samples exists but is excluded from transfer. Author repo README identifies this paper.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://arxiv.org/html/2404.19756v5, architecture section defines compositions of matrix-valued univariate functions; this supports the entire two-layer sum/function chain, not a generic activation swap.

candidates.title: Deep Lattice Networks and Partial Monotonic Functions
candidates.mechanism: Alternate linear embeddings, one-dimensional piecewise-linear calibrators, ensembles of low-dimensional interpolated lookup tables, and another calibrated lattice layer. Each S-dimensional lattice learns vertex responses and evaluates simplex or hypercube interpolation. Optional monotonic constraints are separate from the lookup-table architecture.
candidates.transfer: Create bounded fixed-slot features from L/C plus mask bits, retain original skip, then use calibrator→embedding→calibrator→small 3- or 4-variable lattice ensemble→calibrator→second lattice ensemble→readout bridge. No monotonic emotion assumption on latent features and no external feature labels; optional shape regularization is not added to task loss.
candidates.novelty_difference: NODE enumerates products of learned threshold decisions along oblivious-tree paths; DLN evaluates local multidimensional interpolation cells with vertex parameters and composes calibrated lookup tables. It is not a tree-depth change or invertible univariate spline coupling.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Locally supported, piecewise multivariate interactions could regularize the evidence-to-readout function while retaining joint configurations rather than only per-coordinate calibration.
candidates.risk: No justified monotonicity exists for learned L/C coordinates, so the paper's primary monotonic guarantee does not transfer. Lattice dimension is exponential; bounded inputs may saturate. Two complete lattice stages are needed to avoid presenting a small calibrator as a method.
candidates.code_evidence: Lattice.call dispatches evaluate_with_simplex_interpolation or evaluate_with_hypercube_interpolation. Companion tensorflow_lattice/python/pwl_calibration_layer.py implements PWLCalibration. TensorFlow Lattice README cites the exact paper; this is author-project code, not a claim that the current API is the 2017 frozen implementation.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/6891-deep-lattice-networks-and-partial-monotonic-functions.pdf, Section 2 and Figure 2 specify the three layer families and their composition; Section 2 separates monotonic and nonmonotonic inputs.

candidates.title: Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks
candidates.mechanism: A sparse multilayer circuit fixes two predecessors per node and learns a categorical mixture over all 16 binary truth-table functions, using continuous real-valued relaxations during training. Inference selects the argmax operator. Output nodes can be grouped and summed. AND/OR/XOR/implication composition is the mechanism, not sigmoid reliability weighting.
candidates.transfer: Encode masked fixed L/C slots and availability into bounded soft predicates, apply 4 sparse circuit layers with coverage-checked fixed wiring, group final neurons into representation coordinates and decode residual. Keep original task head. Evaluate with the source argmax-operator rule; continuous inputs mean this remains a real-valued circuit, so bit-packed inference claims do not apply.
candidates.novelty_difference: NLM propagates predicates across arities using variable permutations and exists/forall reductions; this circuit instead learns truth-table operators in fixed sparse wiring with no quantifiers or object tuples. NODE selects tree tests; RAT-SPN has constrained sums/products for densities. None learns the full Boolean operator library at each circuit node.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Composed exclusive-or and implication-like responses may encode contradictory versus jointly present evidence configurations that dense averaging obscures; learned predicates remain latent, not verified logic facts.
candidates.risk: Soft-to-hard operator mismatch and vanishing gradients are material. Random wiring can disconnect useful inputs; verify coverage and task gradients. This is logic-gate computation, not a revived scalar gating baseline, but semantic rules cannot be claimed without evidence.
candidates.code_evidence: LogicLayer.forward_python gathers two indices per neuron, uses softmax(weights) in train and one_hot(argmax,16) in eval, and invokes bin_op_s. GroupSum.forward is the representation aggregation. No CUDA extension is needed to inspect the Python path.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://papers.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2022/file/0d3496dd0cec77a999c98d35003203ca-Paper-Conference.pdf, Sections 3–4, Table 1, Eqs. 2–3: fixed two-input wiring, 16-operator relaxation and grouped sums.

candidates.title: An evidential classifier based on Dempster-Shafer theory and deep learning
candidates.mechanism: Prototype distances→bounded distance support→prototype distributions over singleton hypotheses plus explicit ignorance mass Ω→iterated Dempster combination with conflict normalization. The source classifier finally makes expected-utility decisions; that task head cannot be transplanted here.
candidates.transfer: A possible readout-only adaptation would build latent hypothesis masses from each active role and expose fused singleton/ignorance/conflict features to a residual bridge. Use vacuous mass m(Ω)=1 for inactive roles. Latent hypotheses must not be called calibrated emotion classes. No source utility head or staged CNN pretraining would be used. Pending until the source discrepancy is resolved.
candidates.novelty_difference: Unlike Gaussian-Wishart routing, SPN marginal likelihoods, or prototype residual sums, the core explicitly represents set-valued ignorance and combines compatible evidence while tracking conflict. Prototype distances alone would not establish novelty.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Explicit distinction between unsupported and conflicting evidence may help readout avoid treating absence as a definite negative observation; this requires a correct combination operator and cannot guarantee uncertainty calibration.
candidates.risk: Author master DS3_Dempster applies m1*m2 + m1*Ω2 + Ω1*m2 to the entire vector including Ω, so Ω receives three product terms, while the separate Ω1Ω2 assembly is commented out. This does not match the standard singleton-plus-Ω formula. Near-total conflict is unstable; correlated OSRAM reads also violate a naive independent-evidence interpretation.
candidates.code_evidence: Read raw libs/ds_layer.py: DS1, DS1_activate, DS2, DS2_omega, DS3_Dempster, DS3_normalize. DS1_activate additionally rescales support by sample maximum. DS3_Dempster lines 107–124 reveal the Ω discrepancy. Repository README identifies the exact paper; verified repository identity is not verified mathematical fidelity.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://tongzheng1992.github.io/pdf_publications/DST/tong2021evidential.pdf explains the DS prototype layer and normalized combination. Need pin a corrected author revision or derive and explicitly test a documented paper-based adaptation before acceptance.

candidates.title: Higher-Order Factorization Machines
candidates.mechanism: Learn low-rank coefficients of interaction monomials with distinct feature indices; arbitrary-order ANOVA interactions admit dynamic-programming evaluation, and variants share factors across orders.
candidates.transfer: Could evaluate order-2/3/4 interactions of fixed masked role projections and feed their vector to a readout bridge, without touching task loss. This proposal is not accepted because it mostly repackages the low-rank multiplicative interaction family the task explicitly excludes.
candidates.novelty_difference: ANOVA excludes repeated feature indices and operates on feature coordinates rather than relation-path tensor multiplication, but this algebraic distinction is insufficient to justify another accepted method under the user's stricter meaningful-mechanism criterion.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Potential higher-order co-occurrence modeling with factor sharing; no basis to claim a benefit over existing multiplicative readouts.
candidates.risk: Misidentifying related polylearn code as the exact HOFM author implementation would overstate provenance; increasing degree also creates unstable magnitudes and correlated monomial features.
candidates.code_evidence: Inspected polylearn README and kernels.py::anova_kernel. README credits Vlad Niculae and the separate ICML 2016 Polynomial Networks paper, supports degrees 2/3, and code raises NotImplementedError for >=4. Therefore this is related inspected code, explicitly NOT verified exact-paper author code.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/1607.07195: arbitrary-order FM interaction evaluation and shared-parameter variants. Rejected on task fit in addition to the unresolved exact-code requirement.

candidates.title: Tensorizing Neural Networks
candidates.mechanism: Factor a dense weight matrix into Tensor-Train cores; tensorize input/output indices, sequentially contract input with each core, then bias and ordinary activation. The contraction still represents a single affine layer before activation.
candidates.transfer: A TT adapter could replace a dense readout projection with reshaped fixed L/C inputs. Not accepted: this is a parameterization/compression substitution, not a new evidence-processing mechanism required by this request.
candidates.nearest_old: withdrawn mutan/block low-rank factorization family; hamburger_nmf_full; ordinary Flat MLP
candidates.novelty_difference: TT factorizes weights, whereas Hamburger/RPCA decompose sample evidence. That distinction is real but does not make a compressed ordinary affine layer a substantive new readout method.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Parameter sharing might reduce overfitting; compression alone is not a justified novel fusion hypothesis here.
candidates.risk: Tensor factor ordering is arbitrary for L/C and could create artificial structure. Small rank can remove useful capacity; larger ranks largely restore the original dense map.
candidates.code_evidence: TTLayer.get_output_for reshapes, T.dot-contracts sequential cores, adds bias, then self.nonlinearity. _generate_orthogonal_tt_cores initializes factors. Exact repo is linked in paper footnote 3.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://papers.neurips.cc/paper/5787-tensorizing-neural-networks.pdf: TT-format dense-layer compression and its computational consequences, not a new evidence-combination algorithm.

candidates.title: Density Modeling of Images using a Generalized Normalization Transformation
candidates.mechanism: Linear transform followed by cross-channel divisive normalization y_i=x_i/(β_i+Σ_jγ_ij|x_j|^α_ij)^ε_i; parameter constraints enforce valid denominators. The original density model trains the full transformation through a Gaussianization/negentropy objective and may cascade stages.
candidates.transfer: Can apply learned dense denominator normalization to masked readout channels without cross-batch statistics, but adding only GDN around an MLP would be a normalization tweak. The defining density-learning workflow would require an excluded additional objective.
candidates.novelty_difference: Full positive cross-channel denominator differs algebraically from GRN, but that is not enough under the user's rejection of lightweight normalization/gating variants when no density-learning mechanism is retained.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Might reduce contrast/amplitude dependencies; Gaussianization benefits cannot be transferred without the source learning objective.
candidates.risk: May suppress meaningful evidence strength. TensorFlow Compression is the paper author's later implementation family, not proof that all 2016 free-exponent settings were used in a new readout adapter.
candidates.code_evidence: GDN.call and alpha/beta/gamma/epsilon parameter interfaces inspected in the author-maintained TensorFlow Compression project. This establishes an available normalization operator, not a complete acceptable module.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://www.cns.nyu.edu/pub/lcv/balle16a-reprint.pdf: generalized normalization transformation and density/Gaussianization training.

candidates.title: Iterative Normalization: Beyond Standardization towards Efficient Whitening
candidates.mechanism: Center channels, form regularized covariance, normalize it by its trace, iterate P←1.5P−0.5P³Σ_normalized, rescale and whiten activations. Original training pools batch/spatial observations and maintains running mean/whitening matrix for evaluation.
candidates.transfer: To obey no cross-batch access, one would need per-example masked head-only covariance and identical train/eval statistics. This substantial sample-axis change is unvalidated; applying it as a normalization wrapper does not satisfy the requested complete-method novelty.
candidates.novelty_difference: Whitening remaps features via inverse square root while SPDNet encodes covariance through BiMap/ReEig/LogEig. Nonetheless this candidate would principally change normalization and repeats the covariance rationale; excluded from accepted count.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: Potentially decorrelates evidence channels; scarce correlated heads may make whitening less useful than the original feature scale.
candidates.risk: Unmodified source violates cross-batch constraint; 8 or few more head observations yield rank-deficient covariance and ridge-dominated behavior. Newton iterations do not justify claiming a distinct full architecture.
candidates.code_evidence: iterative_normalization_py.forward reshapes to group×channels×(batch×spatial), computes mean/covariance, runs matrix_power(P,3) updates and updates running_mean/running_wmat. This verifies the source batch dependence directly.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content_CVPR_2019/papers/Huang_Iterative_Normalization_Beyond_Standardization_Towards_Efficient_Whitening_CVPR_2019_paper.pdf: Newton whitening, groupwise normalization and stochastic normalization disturbance.

candidates.title: Finite Scalar Quantization: VQ-VAE Made Simple
candidates.mechanism: Project to a few latent coordinates, bound each coordinate to a prescribed small range, round using a straight-through gradient, and use the Cartesian product of discrete scalar levels as an implicit codebook. No learned vector-codebook or commitment loss is required.
candidates.transfer: A per-readout projection→FSQ→decoder bottleneck could use task loss alone, but then the only imported mechanism is scalar quantization. Adding a generic encoder/decoder does not turn that into the substantive independent method requested.
candidates.novelty_difference: Hard product-code discretization differs from continuous prototype residual aggregation and learned-token compression, but the transferable core is too small under this task's explicit anti-padding criterion.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: A discrete bottleneck might remove fine perturbations; it may equally erase weak sentiment signals and has no reconstruction guarantee with task supervision alone.
candidates.risk: Straight-through gradients are biased and fixed finite levels saturate. Source image-generative or dense-prediction successes do not establish a benefit for OSRAM readout.
candidates.code_evidence: Author notebook inspected: round_ste; FSQ.bound, FSQ.quantize, codes_to_indexes, indexes_to_codes. Quantize is bound→round_ste→normalization; it contains no extra evidence reasoning stage.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://openreview.net/pdf?id=8ishA3LxN8: FSQ product codebook, dimensional reduction and absence of commitment/entropy losses.

candidates.title: Vector Neurons: A General Framework for SO(3)-Equivariant Networks
candidates.mechanism: Represent channels as 3D vectors and compose rotation-equivariant linear maps, direction-conditioned vector nonlinearities, norm-based normalization, directional pooling and learned frame standardization.
candidates.transfer: Artificially grouping L/C scalar coordinates into triples would fit dimensions but has no demonstrated SO(3) action on these latent features. Therefore no valid migration is proposed and the method is excluded.
candidates.novelty_difference: Rotation-equivariant vector algebra is distinct from dynamic kNN EdgeConv or SPD covariance maps, but distinct algebra is not sufficient when the input symmetry assumption is absent.
candidates.benefit_hypothesis: The source benefit concerns robustness to real spatial rotations. No evidence supports that hypothesis for arbitrary learned audio/text/visual readout coordinates.
candidates.risk: Invented coordinate triples and rotations would impose an unjustified invariance, destroy useful channel identity and potentially overlap a geometry lane without meaningful applicability.
candidates.code_evidence: Author README identifies all authors and exact paper. models/vn_layers.py contains VNLinear, VNLeakyReLU, VNBatchNorm, VNMaxPool and VNStdFeature, confirming a complete geometric framework rather than an ordinary activation swap.
candidates.paper_evidence: https://geometry.stanford.edu/lgl_2024/papers/vector_neuron/vector_neuron.pdf: SO(3)-equivariant point-cloud architecture and its required vector transformation law.
